cards.title: Price increase kit
cards.text: I'm raising prices at [BUSINESS] on [DATE]. What changes: [WHICH SERVICES + BY HOW MUCH]. The honest reason: [REASON]. What stays the same: [WHAT CUSTOMERS KEEP]. Write: 1) a short, warm email under 120 words, 2) a 2-line text for regulars, 3) answers to the 4 questions customers are most likely to ask. Calm, no over-apologizing, no hype.

slides.note: Use your real numbers. Never let the AI guess them.

messages.text:
Business: Paws & Co, dog walking.
Date: March 1.
Change: 30-minute walks go up by [AMOUNT].
Reason: insurance and fuel costs went up.
Same: same walker, photo update after every walk. Clients booked before March 1 keep the old rate through March.

cards.title: Subject: A small change to our walk prices
cards.text:
Hi [NAME],
From March 1, our 30-minute walks will go up by [AMOUNT]. Our insurance and fuel costs have gone up, and we'd rather adjust our price than cut corners.
What doesn't change: the same walker every time, and a photo update after every walk.
Booked before March 1? You keep the current rate through March.
Questions? Just reply. Thank you for trusting us with your dog.
— [YOUR NAME]

cards.title: Text for regulars
cards.text: Hi [NAME]! Heads up: from March 1, 30-min walks go up by [AMOUNT]. Same walker, same photo updates. Questions? Just reply.

cards.title: Why are prices going up?
cards.text: Our insurance and fuel costs went up this year. We'd rather adjust the price than cut corners on your dog's walks.

cards.title: Can I keep the old price?
cards.text: If you're booked before March 1, yes, through the end of March. After that, the new rate applies to everyone.

cards.title: Is anything else changing?
cards.text: No. Same walker, same times, same photo after every walk.

cards.title: What if it doesn't fit my budget?
cards.text: Just tell us. We can look at fewer walks a week together.

items.d: Like the old rate for current bookings.
Keep the FAQ answers open to copy.

caption:
How to announce a price increase to customers: email, text and FAQ answers (AI template)

The email is the easy part. The hard part is answering "why?" over and over. So prepare the whole kit in one go.

Copy this:

"I'm raising prices at [BUSINESS] on [DATE]. What changes: [WHICH SERVICES + BY HOW MUCH]. The honest reason: [REASON]. What stays the same: [WHAT CUSTOMERS KEEP]. Write: 1) a short, warm email under 120 words, 2) a 2-line text for regulars, 3) answers to the 4 questions customers are most likely to ask. Calm, no over-apologizing, no hype."

I tried it for an invented dog-walking business. The email said the reason once, spent more words on what stays the same, and offered current bookings the old rate through March.

Fill in your real numbers yourself. Never let the AI guess them.
